subject: Potential data exposure — request for triage, notify criteria & data slice
messages:
From: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finsecure.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finsecure.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Possible exposure — quick ask on notify window and data slice

Ben —

We detected unusual access activity in a subset of API keys that query embeddings for a small customer cohort. At this stage we can't confirm exfiltration, but indicators point to potential read exposure of customer IDs, partial email hashes, and short prompt snippets for ~120 users.

Can Redwood confirm what your DPA requires for (a) preliminary notification timing and (b) the exact subprocessor notification obligations for a delegated inference pool? We need to know the earliest you will notify customers and what evidence slice you will provide (logs, keys, sample tokens).

We're pushing a forensic snapshot from our side but need to coordinate the slices you can legally and technically provide without violating customer confidentiality—particularly because some data touched EU subjects.

Martin Lopez
CISO, FinSecure
martin.lopez@finsecure.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Possible exposure — quick ask on notify window and data slice

Martin —

Thanks for the heads up and the preliminary indicators. We're mobilising our incident playbook now. High-level answers while we spin up the cross-functional MRP: 

- DPA timing: Redwood's standard DPA (section 6.2) requires "prompt" notification and a follow-up with confirmed scope within 72 hours for incidents involving personal data. For EU subjects we treat the 72-hour as a target internal SLO; we will escalate if there's evidence of exfiltration.
- Subprocessor obligations: For delegated inference pools (Dedicated/Private variants), Redwood must notify our direct customer and, where contractually obligated, disclose actions taken with subprocessors. We will not disclose other customers' data in any slice.
- Evidence slice: we can provide time-bounded logs (request IDs, timestamps, truncated token spans), per-request metadata (model, seq length), and a compact forensic snapshot for affected tenant IDs. We need FinSecure to specify the tenant identifiers or a hashed list to narrow scope.

Immediate asks from our side: 
1) Please share the hashed identifiers or a short allowlist for the cohort you believe affected.
2) Any regulatory triggers we should prioritize (e.g., explicit GDPR data subject complaints).
3) Confirm whether you'd like a live Zoom with engineering and our forensic team in the next 2 hours.

Cc'ing our privacy (Grace) and legal (Marissa) to align on what we can produce under current contracts.

Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finsecure.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Possible exposure — quick ask on notify window and data slice

Martin / Ben —

We're standing up the forensic snapshot process. Operational notes and what we need from FinSecure to produce a minimized evidence set: 

- We will capture: request_id, request_timestamp (UTC), upstream IP block (anonymized to /24), model variant, input prefix (first 64 chars redacted), token counts, and the decision trace for any policy blocks. We will NOT include full prompt bodies or full output tokens in the initial slice.
- To accelerate: provide a list of up to 200 hashed customer IDs (SHA256) or a regex pattern for internal tenant IDs. If you cannot share hashes, supply a start/end timestamp window and any sample request_ids you have.
- Legal constraints: Per our DPA and mutual confidentiality clauses, we can only include data tied to the affected FinSecure tenant(s). Cross-tenant data will be redacted.

Attachments I will produce once we have FinSecure's selector: forensic_snapshot_20260810.tar.gz (encrypted), chain_of_custody_finsecure.pdf (signed). See provisional attachment list below — I will push when ready.

Technical contact for the snapshot: kimberly_park@redwood.com (forensic lead).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finsecure.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finsecure.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 18:41:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Possible exposure — quick ask on notify window and data slice

Kimberly —

Thanks. We can provide a hashed list (SHA256) for 137 affected users and a narrower timestamp window: 2026-08-09T22:00:00Z to 2026-08-10T04:00:00Z. We are not asking for full prompt bodies — just the truncated input prefix and request_ids for correlation.

Regulatory triggers: this includes EU data subjects; we need to treat GDPR notification cadence as priority. We are prepared to share a redacted sample of two request_ids now in a separate secure message.

We agree to an initial provisional notification to the impacted customers' legal contacts within 48 hours with a statement that the investigation is ongoing and forensic artifacts will follow within 72 hours after scope confirmation. Does Redwood have any objections to that cadence?

Martin

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Possible exposure — quick ask on notify window and data slice

Martin —

Appreciate the hashed list — please send via the secure channel (we'll accept the file upload link or encrypted email). We do not object to your proposed cadence (48h provisional; 72h forensic follow-up) provided our teams agree on the final scope within 24 hours so we can meet our DPA SLOs.

Next steps we commit to now: 
- Redwood will prepare the encrypted forensic snapshot and chain-of-custody doc within 48 hours of scope confirmation.
- We will produce a minimal evidence slice (request_ids + truncated input prefix + timestamps + model metadata) for the hashed cohort you provide.
- Legal will draft a provisional notification template for you to review before customer outreach.

I'll schedule a 30-minute bridge for 10:30 AM (ET) today with our forensic lead (Kimberly) and Marissa from Legal to lock scope and agree handover mechanics. If that time doesn't work for your team, propose alternatives.

Ben
